detail.title: Refined Coarse-Grained Dissipation Bounds and Finite Relaxation
detail.summary: This revision formalizes the role of nonreciprocal coupling and trajectory-based inference in defining lower bounds on entropy production. It highlights how information engines leverage feedback and internal state statistics to modulate dissipation, distinguishing between driven particle contributions and passive degree-of-freedom influences.
detail.reason: Updates findings with new evidence regarding nonreciprocal coupling (source-cd8bfc44e8eb4729) and theoretical frameworks for causal models (peer-fbcb6597c1b7daa2cd530707).

detail.title: Predictive Information and Dissipation Bounds
detail.question: What is the theoretical relationship between predictive information and thermodynamic dissipation in nonequilibrium systems with finite or noisy memory?
detail.reason: Continuing the active project within the enforced predictive_dissipation topic.

detail.title: Predictive Information and Dissipation in Information Engines
detail.summary: This research entry synthesizes current bounds on dissipation in nonequilibrium systems, focusing on how information-theoretic constraints on predictive memory limit thermodynamic efficiency. We evaluate the role of nonreciprocal coupling and state statistics in shaping these dissipation limits.
